home.heroDescription: Access the university's official training modules for Fundamentals of Computer Science.

turing.title: Turing Machines
turing.description: Learn about the fundamentals of computation through Turing Machines and their transition functions. Explore the limits of what can be computed.
turing.overviewText: A Turing Machine is a mathematical model of computation that defines an abstract machine which manipulates symbols on a strip of tape according to a table of rules. It provides a simple yet powerful framework for understanding what problems can be solved algorithmically.
turing.exercise1Desc: Design a simple TM transition table
turing.exercise3Desc: Find the maximum output for n-state TMs
turing.exercise4Desc: Prove undecidability of the halting problem

automata.title: Finite Automata
automata.description: Study deterministic and non-deterministic finite automata. Learn how to design, minimize, and convert between different automata representations.
automata.overviewText: Finite Automata are the simplest computational models used to recognize patterns. They consist of states, transitions, and accept/reject decisions. DFAs and NFAs form the foundation for lexical analysis, pattern matching, and regular expression engines.
automata.exercise1Desc: Create a DFA that accepts strings ending in '01'
automata.exercise2Desc: Design an NFA for a given regular expression

number.title: Number Systems
number.description: Master conversions between Binary, Octal, Decimal, and Hexadecimal. Understand IEEE 754 floating-point representation.
number.overviewText: Number systems are fundamental to how computers store and process data. Understanding binary, octal, and hexadecimal representations is essential for low-level programming, networking, and digital design.
number.ex_u03_binAddDesc: Convert two decimal numbers to binary and add them.
number.ex_u04_binToHexOctDesc: Convert 8-bit binary numbers to hex and octal.
number.ex_u05_floatToBinDesc: Convert simple floating point numbers to binary.
number.ex_u05_ieeeEncodeDesc: Convert float values to the 32-bit IEEE 754 standard.
number.ex_u05_ieeeDecodeDesc: Calculate the decimal value of an IEEE 754 32-bit string.
number.examplesFallback: Interactive examples for Number Systems will be available here.

moore.title: Moore & Mealy Machines
moore.description: Explore sequential circuit design with Moore and Mealy state machines. Learn the differences and when to apply each model.
moore.overviewText: Moore and Mealy machines are finite state machines with output. In Moore machines, output depends only on the current state. In Mealy machines, output depends on both the current state and the current input. Both are fundamental to digital circuit design.
moore.exercise1Desc: Create a sequence detector as Moore machine
moore.exercise2Desc: Create a sequence detector as Mealy machine
moore.exercise3Desc: Convert a Moore machine to equivalent Mealy
moore.exercise4Desc: Convert a Mealy machine to equivalent Moore

dnf.title: Disjunctive Normal Form
dnf.description: Learn to convert boolean expressions into DNF. Practice with truth tables, Karnaugh maps, and logical simplification techniques.
dnf.overviewText: Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF) is a standardized way of writing boolean expressions as a disjunction (OR) of conjunctions (AND). Every boolean function can be expressed in DNF, making it a universal representation for logical circuits and decision-making systems.
dnf.exercise1Desc: Derive the DNF from a given truth table
dnf.exercise2Desc: Simplify a boolean function using K-maps
dnf.exercise3Desc: Draw the logic circuit for a given DNF

java.title: Java Programming
java.description: Work with core Java basics such as console output, loops, and arrays. The simulation tab provides a directly editable Java code editor.
java.overviewText: This topic introduces simple Java programs step by step. The focus is on the Main class, the main method, console output, loops, and small array-based tasks.
java.example1Text: The smallest Java program with a main method and a console print statement.
java.example2Text: A for loop is the standard way to repeat the same instruction several times.
java.example3Text: An integer array can be sorted in ascending order with Arrays.sort.
java.exercise1Desc: Write a Java program that prints Hello World to the console exactly once.
java.exercise2Desc: Use a loop to print Hello World to the console exactly five times.
java.exercise3Desc: Add two integer values and print the sum in the console.
java.exercise4Desc: Sort an integer array in ascending order and print the result afterwards.
java.exercise5Desc: Iterate over an array and determine the largest contained value.

addition.desc: Positional addition in binary. Adding two ones creates a carry to the next position.
addition.carryOutWarning: Warning: A carry has exceeded the 8th bit (Carry Out).
addition.overflowWarning: Overflow error! The addition of logically positive numbers resulted in a negative two's complement result.

subtraction.desc: Binary subtraction is usually performed as addition with the negative number (in two's complement).
subtraction.step3: 3. Add the two's complement to Number A
subtraction.carryOutInfo: Since we subtract via two's complement, a carry-out usually means the result is positive. We just discard the carry in this fixed-point system.

multiplication.stepDesc: Bit {{n}} ({{bit}}) = 1, so multiplicand {{val}} shifted left by {{shift}} = {{result}}

division.desc: Written division by trial (go from left to right).
division.stepDesc: Step {{n}}: {{current}} >= {{divisor}}, so 1 to quotient and subtract {{divisor}}

shifting.desc: Here you can shift binary numbers to the left or right.
shifting.shiftLeftExpl: A left shift by n positions corresponds to a multiplication by 2^n.
shifting.shiftRightExpl: A right shift by n positions corresponds to a division by 2^n (without remainder).
shifting.leftStepsTitle: Left Shift: Zeros are appended on the right
shifting.rightStepsTitle: Right Shift: Bits fall off on the right
shifting.stepLeftShift: Bits shift left. A {{count}} zero is appended.
shifting.stepRightComplete: All {{count}} right bits have been removed.
shifting.stepRightZero: Shift by {{count}} >= length of number, result is 0.

ieee754.desc: Addition of two 32-bit floating-point numbers according to IEEE 754.
ieee754.shiftBitDesc: Shift {{n}}: Bit moved to the right.
ieee754.mantissaShifted: The mantissa of the smaller number is shifted to the right by {{diff}} places.
ieee754.expAligned: Now both operands have the exponent 2^{{exp}} and can be added (or subtracted).
ieee754.normBack: The result is converted back into the format 1.M × 2^E.
ieee754.shiftDesc: The mantissa of the smaller number is shifted to the right by {{diff}} places.
ieee754.addDesc: Now both operands have the exponent 2^{{exp}} and can be added.
ieee754.normDesc: The result is converted back into the format 1.M × 2^E.

compare.desc: Compares two binary numbers bit by bit from left to right.
compare.pad: The numbers are padded to the same length (with zeros on the left).
compare.resultEq: The numbers are equal in size.
compare.resultGreater: Number A is greater than Number B.
compare.resultLess: Number A is less than Number B.
compare.padDesc: The numbers are padded to the same length (with leading zeros):
compare.stepEqual: Position {{pos}}: Both bits are {{bit}}, continue to next bit.
compare.stepResultGreater: At position {{pos}}: A has 1, B has 0 → A is greater than B.
compare.stepResultLess: At position {{pos}}: A has 0, B has 1 → A is less than B.
compare.finalResultNote: Since a difference was found here, the comparison is complete. Further bits are no longer considered.

numbers.sameBase: Input and target base are identical.
numbers.lockedDesc: Click the button to show the result and calculation steps.
numbers.enterValue: Enter a number to see the calculation steps.
numbers.decToBinDesc: The number is continuously divided by base 2. The remainders, read from bottom to top, give the binary number.
numbers.divByBaseDesc: The number is continuously divided by base {{base}}. The remainders, read from bottom to top, give the result.
numbers.binToDecDesc: Each digit is multiplied by the corresponding power of base 2 and added.
numbers.otherToDecDesc: The conversion works analogously with the sum of powers to the given base.
numbers.invalidRange: Please enter a value between -128 and +127.
numbers.enterValueForExp: Enter a valid number for explanation.
numbers.positiveExplanation: Positive numbers are represented the same way as regular binary numbers. A sign bit (first bit) of 0 indicates the number is positive.
numbers.howTwosBuilt: How the number {{val}} is formed as 8-bit Two's Complement:
numbers.zeroToOne: All zeros become ones, all ones become zeros:
numbers.zeroDesc: Exponent and mantissa are logically 0. There is a +0 and -0, depending on the sign bit.
numbers.infDesc: Exponent consists of all ones (255), mantissa is 0. Sign decides between +Inf and -Inf.
numbers.nanDesc: Exponent consists of all ones (255), mantissa is non-zero. Represents invalid operations like 0/0.
numbers.specialCaseNoMath: There is no regular calculation steps for special cases. The representation is defined in the standard (see special cases box).
numbers.normDesc: Convert the number to binary and shift the comma until exactly one 1 is in front of the comma.
numbers.normSubDesc: The comma was shifted such that the exponent y = {{val}}.
numbers.biasDesc: The IEEE 754 standard adds a bias of 127 to the actual exponent to store negative exponents without a sign.
numbers.mantissaDesc: The mantissa stores the decimal places after normalization.
numbers.hiddenBitDesc: Because normalization ensures there is always a 1 before the comma (except for 0), this 1 is not stored to save 1 bit of space.
numbers.nonDecConvHint: Conversion between two non-decimal bases is easiest using decimal as an intermediate step.
numbers.howSignBuilt: How the number {{val}} is formed in Sign-Magnitude:
numbers.setSignBit: The first bit (leftmost) is set to 1 to represent a negative number:
numbers.howOnesBuilt: How the number {{val}} is formed as 8-bit One's Complement:
numbers.expBinToDecDesc: The 8-bit exponent is read as an unsigned integer and the bias (127) is subtracted:
numbers.mantissaBinToDecDesc: The actual mantissa value is calculated using the implicit 'hidden bit' (1 + fraction value). Each bit n after the comma is multiplied by 2^(-n):
numbers.finalFormulaDesc: For the final decimal number, the sign, actual mantissa, and exponent factor are multiplied together:

config.title: Turing Machine Configuration
config.cannotRemoveBlank: The blank symbol cannot be removed.
config.cannotRemoveSymbolColumn: The symbol column cannot be removed.
config.cannotRemoveLastState: At least one state column must remain.
config.symbolSingleChar: Tape symbols must consist of exactly one character.
config.symbolDuplicate: This tape symbol already exists in the transition table.
config.transitionCellInvalid: Transitions must use the format (Next State, Write Symbol, Movement) and the write symbol must be exactly one character.

validation.statesEmpty: At least one state must be defined.
validation.initialStateMissing: The initial state '{{state}}' must exist in the set of states.
validation.haltStatesEmpty: At least one halt state must be defined.
validation.haltStateMissing: The halt state '{{state}}' must exist in the set of states.
validation.blankSymbolMissing: The blank symbol '{{symbol}}' must be part of the tape alphabet.
validation.blankSymbolInvalid: The blank symbol '{{symbol}}' must consist of exactly one character.
validation.tapeSymbolInvalid: Tape alphabet symbol '{{symbol}}' must consist of exactly one character.
validation.initialTapeInvalidSymbol: Initial tape symbol '{{symbol}}' must be part of the input alphabet and consist of exactly one character.
validation.transitionReadSymbolMissing: A transition is defined for read symbol '{{symbol}}', but this symbol is not part of the tape alphabet.
validation.transitionReadSymbolInvalid: Transition read symbol '{{symbol}}' must consist of exactly one character.
validation.transitionStateMissing: A transition is defined for state '{{state}}', but this state is not part of the set of states.
validation.transitionNextStateMissing: Transition from state '{{state}}' on symbol '{{symbol}}' points to unknown next state '{{nextState}}'.
validation.transitionWriteSymbolMissing: Transition from state '{{state}}' on symbol '{{symbol}}' writes unknown symbol '{{writeSymbol}}'.
validation.transitionWriteSymbolInvalid: Transition from state '{{state}}' on symbol '{{symbol}}' must write exactly one character.
